title: SDK failure-mode guidance for streaming toolflow (PRD draft)
content:
Context:
This PRD draft defines SDK ergonomics and runtime behaviour for failure-mode-aware streaming tool calls and structured output. Goal: give product and SDK teams a single operational model to reason about partial streams, tool-call retries/hedging, and deterministic resumability while preserving developer ergonomics and minimizing accidental complexity for integrators.

Problems we see in the wild:
- Unclear semantics when a tool-call times out mid-stream: clients either drop state or buffer indefinitely.
- Developers need simple primitives but also observable hooks for failure cases (network, model fallback, tool error, quota).
- SDKs often conflate retrying entire session vs. retrying a single tool invocation, causing duplicate side effects.
- Structured output schemas break when partial fragments are delivered; clients lack light-weight merge strategies.

Key proposals (high level):
1) Failure-mode taxonomy (SDK + runtime signals)
   - TransientNetwork: ephemeral network blip; intent preserved, resume possible
   - CapacityFallback: serving runtime switched model variant for latency/cost reasons
   - ToolTimeout: external tool (e.g. DB call, function execution) failed to respond in hedged window
   - ToolTransientError: tool returned 5xx / retriable error (idempotency uncertain)
   - ToolPermanentError: unrecoverable business error (validation, permissions)
   - SessionDrift: client session state diverged (resumed on a different route)

   Each taxonomy value maps to recommended SDK behavior and recommended server signals.

2) SDK surface primitives (minimal, composable)
   - StreamingCall.start(streamOpts) -> streamHandle (exposes onFragment, onError, onResume)
   - streamHandle.attachTool(toolSpec) -> toolHandle (encapsulates idempotency token + side-effect policy)
   - toolHandle.call(args) -> returns ToolCallFuture with events: toolStart, toolPartialFragment, toolComplete, toolError
   - PrefetchProfile (named presets): {aggressive, balanced, conservative} exported by SDK for opt-in prefetch behavior
   - HedgingPolicy: lightweight policy object: {hedgeWindowMs, maxHedgedReplicas, idempotency: "safe|unsafe|compensating"}
   - MergeHints: developer-supplied hints for partial structured outputs (merge strategy: append/patch/last-wins)
3) Failure-mode behavioral rules (mapping taxonomy -> behavior)
   - TransientNetwork: SDK buffers up to N fragments, retries transport handshake; onResume, replays uncommitted fragments to consumer with 'replay' metadata.
   - CapacityFallback: runtime emits compatible-model hint; SDK alerts developer callback with 'fallback_profile' and continues stream.
   - ToolTimeout + ToolTransientError: SDK triggers hedging if ToolSpec.idempotency=="safe" and HedgingPolicy allows; otherwise surface error to client and expose rollback hooks.
   - ToolPermanentError: surface human-readable error with structured code, abort tool-specific branch but keep outer stream alive where possible.
   - SessionDrift: SDK emits session-cohort token and suggests session revalidation; expose a short-circuit api reattach(sessionToken)

4) Observability contract (what we must emit)
   - Mandatory metrics (per-call): stream_latency_p50/p95, toolcall_latency_p50/p95, toolcall_error_rate, hedged_toolcalls_count, resume_count, partial_fragments_emitted
   - Traces: every toolcall produces a span with tags: failure_mode, hedged, idempotency
   - Event hooks: on_stream_replay, on_tool_hedge_start, on_tool_hedge_resolution, on_tool_compensation_invoked
   - Telemetry-first design: default SDK behavior should send summarized telemetry with low overhead; devs can opt into verbose mode for debugging.

5) Structured output and partial fragments
   - Introduce small envelope on fragment: {fragment_id, sequence_index, committed: bool, schema_version, merge_hint}
   - SDK provides MergeStrategies implementable in userland but ships with sane defaults: "transactional-snapshot", "append-safe", "patch-merge".
   - When committed==false, SDK treats fragment as speculative; on commit event (server-sent) the fragment becomes authoritative.

6) Safety & side-effects (tool calling)
   - ToolSpec must include: alpha idempotency token (optional), side_effect_policy: ["no-op-safe","compensating","must-not-retry"]
   - If must-not-retry and runtime suggests hedging, SDK should refuse to hedge and surface a clear failure result with documentation link.
   - For compensating operations, SDK exposes compensation helpers and a standard compensation webhook signature.

7) Developer ergonomics: examples and flows
   - Simple fast-path (no hedging): developer calls streamingClient.start({profile:"balanced"}).attachTool({name:"lookup",idempotency:"safe"}).call(args)
     SDK handles tool wiring, exposes simple onPartial fragment callback, commit events handled automatically.
   - Advanced: long-running side-effectful tool: attach side_effect_policy:"compensating" and register compensation handler: onCompensate(context) -> promise. SDK will coordinate compensation on conflict.

8) Rollout & compatibility plan
   - Backwards compatibility: default SDK must behave exactly like existing streaming API when devs do not opt into failure-mode features. Opt-ins are per-call flags: {failureModeAware:true}
   - Server rollout phases: feature-flag initial telemetry (2 weeks), hedging runtime disabled; enable runtime hedging in canary (traffic slice 5%) with SDK canary release; full enable on passing thresholds.

9) Acceptance criteria (initial)
   - SDK reference implementation (JS + Python) exposes new primitives and passes compatibility suite against older clients.
   - Simulated failure tests: transient network, tool timeout, capacity fallback — SDK shows correct replay/hedging behavior in 95% of test permutations.
   - Observability: metrics appear in prometheus/telemetry pipeline and trace spans carry failure_mode tag.

10) Experiment matrix (what to measure):
   - Developer friction (time-to-integrate) in a small sample of customers using new API vs old (A/B)
   - Reduction in duplicate side-effects for hedged-safe flows
   - Increase in success-perceived-latency for hedged flows vs. cost delta (tokens + compute)
   - False-positive hedges causing business errors (should be zero for must-not-retry flows)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Naming: do we call the primitive "HedgingPolicy" or "SpeculativeReplicaPolicy"?
- Should MergeHints accept executable JS/Python merge functions shipped by developers, or only declarative strategies? Security concern.
- UX for mobile: how large should SDK buffer be on constrained environments? default conservative profile needed.
- Telemetry privacy: sample-rate by default 0.1 for verbose traces; is that ok for enterprise compliance?

Implementation tasks (initial):
- [ ] Draft SDK API surface docs and lightweight reference JS impl (owner: Diego) — 2 sprints
- [ ] Runtime: emit failure_mode and compatible_model_hint (owner: Serving Runtime team) — 3 sprints
- [ ] Observability: add hedged_toolcalls_count and resume_count to metrics catalog (owner: Observability) — 1 sprint
- [ ] QA: build adversarial failure harness for streaming+tool mocks (owner: SRE/QA) — 2 sprints

Appendix: short sample SDK pseudo-code (JS-like)

const s = StreamingClient.start({profile: 'balanced', failureModeAware:true})
const t = s.attachTool({name:'charge-card', idempotency:'safe', side_effect_policy:'compensating'})
t.call({card, amount})
  .on('toolPartialFragment', f => renderPartial(f))
  .on('toolComplete', r => commitApplicationState(r))
  .on('toolError', e => {
    if (e.failure_mode === 'ToolTimeout' && t.idempotency==='safe') {
      // SDK automatically attempted a hedged retry; we surface resolution with e.hedgeResolution
    }
  })

Notes for SDK implementers: keep default API simple. Opt-in flags should be obvious in docs. Log human-friendly messages for failure events; developers will copy them into product error UIs.

Document history:
- Drafted by: Asha Mehta (product)
- Inputs: internal recordings with Solutions Eng, field incidents, Serving Runtime hedging experiments
- Next review: November product sync (2025-11-21)
summary: Draft PRD describing failure-mode-aware SDK and runtime features for streaming + tool-calling. Introduces a taxonomy of failures, SDK primitives (HedgingPolicy, PrefetchProfile, MergeHints), observability and rollout plan, sample SDK pseudo-code, and experiment/acceptance criteria.
